title: Simultaneous EEG and fMRI signals during sleep from humans
description: This dataset comprises simultaneous EEG and fMRI recordings from 33 healthy human participants during sleep and wakefulness, collected at Pennsylvania State University. The study includes resting-state sessions before and after a visual-motor adaptation task, followed by multiple sleep sessions with polysomnographic staging. The synchronized acquisition of high-density EEG (32 channels) and BOLD fMRI signals enables investigation of the neural correlates of sleep-wake transitions and autonomic-neural interactions during sleep.
methods_description: EEG data were collected using a 32-channel MR-compatible EEG system (Brain Products, Munich, Germany) synchronized with BOLD fMRI acquisition. Each scanning session included an anatomical scan, two 10-minute resting-state sessions (before and after a visual-motor adaptation task), and multiple 15-minute sleep sessions. Sleep stages were scored for 30-second epochs across all sessions.
